acceptance_criteria.criterion: The project compiles cleanly under `dotnet build -c Release` with zero warnings under the inherited `TreatWarningsAsErrors=true`.
`AppOptions` exposes nested `Logging`, `Appearance`, `Window`, and `ExternalTools` members whose property names match the documented `appsettings.json` schema exactly.
The project contains no references to Avalonia, Microsoft.Extensions.*, Serilog, or any I/O-performing API.

summary: Created src/VideoIndexer.Core/VideoIndexer.Core.csproj targeting net8.0 with no package references.
Created AppOptions, LoggingOptions, AppearanceOptions, WindowOptions, ExternalToolsOptions records matching the documented appsettings.json schema.
Created IAppPaths, ISettingsService, IThemeService interfaces in VideoIndexer.Core.Abstractions namespace.
Created ThemeMode enum (System, Light, Dark) in VideoIndexer.Core.Enums namespace.
dotnet build -c Release succeeds with zero warnings under TreatWarningsAsErrors=true.

comments.note: AppearanceOptions.Theme is typed as ThemeMode enum but appsettings.json stores it as a string (e.g., 'System'). The configuration binder will handle string-to-enum conversion automatically, but this dependency is implicit. Consider adding a JSON converter attribute or documentation note to make the expectation explicit.

ISettingsService.SaveAsync returns Task but the interface has no LoadAsync. If settings are reloaded at runtime (e.g., reloadOnChange in IConfiguration), callers have no async notification path through this interface. The Current property will become stale silently. A change-notification mechanism (event or IObservable) should be considered for a future WP.

Option records live in VideoIndexer.Core.Options namespace, abstractions in VideoIndexer.Core.Abstractions. ThemeMode enum is in VideoIndexer.Core.Enums. This is clean; ensure all downstream projects follow the same namespace pattern for their types.

summary: Reviewed all 10 implementation files: VideoIndexer.Core.csproj, 5 option records, ThemeMode enum, and 3 abstractions.
All four acceptance criteria are met. No blocking issues found.
One non-idiomatic pattern noted (EventHandler<ThemeMode>) and two documentation-forward items raised. No Fix-Forward changes applied — code was already correct and clean.

Architecture is sound: pure abstractions with no infrastructure dependencies, sealed records with init-only properties, full nullable annotation, CancellationToken on SaveAsync. Suitable foundation for dependent WPs.

comments.note: IThemeService.ThemeChanged is typed EventHandler<ThemeMode> (i.e., EventHandler<TEventArgs> where TEventArgs is an enum). This is syntactically valid since .NET 4.5 removed the EventArgs constraint, but it is non-idiomatic. Standard .NET convention expects TEventArgs to derive from EventArgs. No implementations exist yet, so WP-003/004 should use the same pattern consistently. If consistency with BCL conventions is desired in the future, a thin ThemeModeChangedEventArgs : EventArgs wrapper would be idiomatic — however this does not warrant blocking the current WP.

LoggingOptions.Verbosity uses integer levels 1–4 documented in a comment (1=Warning, 2=Information, 3=Debug, 4=Verbose). This is an implicit enum over a plain int. Future WPs or the Documentation agent should ensure the appsettings.json schema doc explicitly maps these levels, or a dedicated LogVerbosity enum should be considered when the logging infrastructure is implemented (WP-003/004). Not blocking — the comment is sufficient for the Core layer.

ISettingsService exposes SaveAsync but no LoadAsync. As noted by the Developer, the Current property may silently become stale if reload-on-change is active. A change-notification mechanism (event or IObservable<AppOptions>) should be tracked as a future enhancement. Not blocking for this WP.

[documentation-forward] ISettingsService.Current property lacks a doc comment clarifying whether it reflects the last persisted state or the last loaded state, and that it does not auto-update on external file changes. Add a <remarks> block so that implementation authors know the expected contract.

[documentation-forward] LoggingOptions.Verbosity integer-to-level mapping (1=Warning..4=Verbose) should be reflected in the appsettings.json schema documentation (plan or README) so users know valid values without reading the source code.

[documentation-forward] WindowOptions properties Width, Height, and Maximized have no XML doc comments. AppearanceOptions.Language has a BCP-47 example in its comment but no note on fallback behaviour when an unsupported tag is supplied. These gaps should be addressed before API documentation is generated.
